studyPages.body:
WHY REPRODUCTION MATTERS
====

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
----
• Explain why reproduction matters in your own words.
• Give a real Kenyan example that shows why reproduction matters.
• Avoid a common mistake learners make about why reproduction matters.

INTRODUCTION
----
Around a hardware shop in Nakuru, learners meet science ideas without opening a textbook. 2.3 Reproduction in Human Beings. This page explains why reproduction matters so you can recognise it, name it correctly, and use it safely.

MAIN NOTES
----
• 2.3 Reproduction in Human Beings.
• Menstrual cycle consists of natural changes that occur to the body of a female human being every month in preparatio to pregnancy.
• A menstrual cycle lasts between 28-35 days. However, this can vary between female and from one cycle to the next. The cycle depends on hormones.
• Hormones are chemical messengers in the body.
• They direct the body on what to do and when to do it.
• The menstrual cycle is a process controlled by hormones in the female body.  The menstrual cycle is divided in to the following phases:.
• Bleeding from the vagina begins. This is caused by the loss of the lining of the uterus.

MAIN NOTES
----
• This is called menstruation or monthly periods.
• The lining of the uterus begins to regrow and an ovum starts to mature in one of the ovaries.
• The ovum travels through the oviduct towards the uterus.
• If the egg becomes fertilized by a sperm and attaches itself to the uterus wall, the woman becomes pregnant.

MAIN NOTES
----
• This is called menstruation or monthly periods.
• If the circle length falls in the normal range but varies by 7 to 9 days from the cycle to cycle that is a sign of an irregular period too.
• For example, if one is 25 days and the next is 33 days, your cycles would be considered irregular.
• Sperms swim through the cervix into the uterus up to the oviduct.
• The zygote moves from the oviduct and enters the uterus, attaching itself to the uterus walls.
• In some cases, some females may fail to get periods.

MAIN NOTES
----
• Fertilization is the fusion of a sperm with an ovum in the oviduct (also called the fallopian tube.).
